communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Untitled
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear Ventura County Public Records Coordinator:
Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Government Code § 7920.000 et seq., I request copies of public records concerning Ventura County and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office (“VCSO”) acquisition, installation, operation, administration, use, oversight, and sharing of information obtained through Flock Safety automated license plate recognition (“ALPR”) cameras and related Flock Safety technology.

For purposes of this request, “Flock/ALPR information” includes information collected through Flock Safety cameras, ALPR systems, Flock Safety software and databases, and any related vehicle-location, license-plate, vehicle-characteristic, alert, or investigative information.

This request includes Flock/ALPR systems operated, owned, leased, funded, administered, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO, including systems located in unincorporated areas of the County, County Service Areas, and other areas where the County or VCSO has responsibility for or access to the system.
It also includes records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's access to Flock systems or Flock/ALPR information maintained by another governmental agency, private entity, municipality, school, business, neighborhood organization, or other third party.
1. Contracts, agreements, and financial records
All contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding, purchase orders, invoices, amendments, renewals, extensions, proposals, quotes, statements of work, and other agreements between Ventura County, VCSO, or any County department and Flock Group, Inc., Flock Safety, or any related Flock entity.
All records concerning the County's initial acquisition or implementation of Flock Safety ALPR technology, including Board of Supervisors agenda materials, staff reports, recommendations, presentations, resolutions, approvals, and related documentation.
All records concerning the acquisition or implementation of Flock cameras through County Service Areas, Municipal Advisory Councils, grant-funded programs, Sheriff's Office programs, or other County-administered programs.
All records reflecting the total cost of the Flock program, including installation, equipment, software, licensing, subscriptions, maintenance, replacement, upgrades, cellular/data service, storage, and other associated costs.
All invoices and payment records relating to Flock Safety from the beginning of the County's relationship with Flock through the date this request is processed.
All records concerning grants, state or federal funding, donations, private funding, County Service Area funds, or other sources used to acquire or operate Flock cameras.
All records concerning any proposal, quote, bid, solicitation, procurement, or competitive process relating to the acquisition of Flock technology.
2. Number, location, and operation of cameras
Records identifying the total number of Flock Safety ALPR cameras currently operated, owned, leased, funded, or otherwise controlled by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying the location of each Flock camera, including installation addresses, intersections, street locations, geographic coordinates, or other location information sufficient to identify where each camera is installed.
Records identifying the date each camera was installed, activated, deactivated, relocated, replaced, or removed.
Records identifying the type and model of each Flock camera or device currently or previously deployed by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records identifying which cameras are located within incorporated municipalities but are accessible by, operated by, funded by, or otherwise connected to Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning any proposed expansion, reduction, relocation, replacement, or modification of the County's Flock camera network.
3. Policies, procedures, and legal authority
The County's and VCSO's current and all prior Flock Safety/ALPR usage and privacy policies.
All policies, directives, general orders, standard operating procedures, training materials, manuals, instructions, or other documents governing the access, search, use, retention, sharing, dissemination, or deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the County official, Sheriff, employee, unit, or other person responsible for custody, administration, oversight, or implementation of the County's Flock/ALPR information.
All records identifying the job classifications, positions, units, employees, contractors, or other persons authorized to access Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning training required or provided to personnel who have access to Flock/ALPR information, including privacy, civil liberties, data security, ALPR operation, appropriate-use, and data-sharing training.
All legal opinions, memoranda, analyses, correspondence, or other records concerning the legality or constitutionality of the County's or VCSO's use of Flock Safety ALPR technology.
All records concerning compliance with California Civil Code §§ 1798.90.5–1798.90.55 and any other applicable California or federal law governing ALPR technology or surveillance systems.
4. Board of Supervisors, public approval, and public notice
All Ventura County Board of Supervisors agenda packets, staff reports, presentations, minutes, recordings, resolutions, ordinances, notices, and other records concerning the County's decision to implement, continue, expand, renew, or modify its Flock ALPR program.
All records concerning public meetings of the Board of Supervisors, Municipal Advisory Councils, County Service Areas, or other County bodies at which Flock Safety or ALPR technology was discussed.
All records concerning opportunities provided to the public to comment on implementation or operation of the County's ALPR program.
All records identifying the date and meeting at which the governing body provided or considered public comment concerning implementation of the ALPR system.
All correspondence received from members of the public concerning Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
5. ALPR searches and access
Records sufficient to show the number of searches or queries conducted through the County's Flock system, broken down by month, from the beginning of the program through the date this request is processed.
Records sufficient to show the number of Flock/ALPR searches conducted by each authorized user, employee, unit, department, or agency, to the extent such information is maintained.
Records of access to ALPR information maintained pursuant to California Civil Code § 1798.90.52, including the date and time of access, query terms or data elements used, username or identifying information of the person conducting the search, affiliated organization, and stated purpose for the search.
Records concerning audits, reviews, investigations, or monitoring of employee or contractor access to Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any unauthorized, improper, excessive, or suspected misuse of the Flock/ALPR system or its data.
All records concerning complaints, disciplinary actions, investigations, or corrective actions involving improper access or use of Flock/ALPR information.
6. Data retention and deletion
Records establishing the County's current retention period for Flock/ALPR information.
All policies, procedures, technical settings, contractual provisions, or other records governing the retention and deletion of Flock/ALPR information.
Records sufficient to establish whether Flock/ALPR data is automatically deleted after a specified period and, if so, the applicable retention period.
Records concerning any exceptions to the County's standard retention period, including circumstances in which data is retained because it is associated with an investigation, criminal case, evidence, warrant, subpoena, litigation hold, or other legal purpose.
Records sufficient to show the volume or amount of ALPR data retained by the County, if such records are maintained.
7. Data sharing and outside access
All records concerning Ventura County's or VCSO's participation in any Flock Safety national, regional, statewide, or multi-agency data-sharing network.
All agreements, memoranda, policies, authorizations, correspondence, or other records concerning sharing of Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data with other law enforcement agencies or public agencies.
Records identifying every outside agency, department, task force, or governmental entity that has been granted access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data or with which Ventura County or VCSO has shared such information.
Records concerning any access by outside agencies to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR data, including records sufficient to identify the agency, date, purpose, and type of access, to the extent maintained.
Records concerning any requests by outside agencies for Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information.
All records concerning any sharing, transfer, disclosure, or access to Flock/ALPR information by federal law-enforcement agencies or federal governmental entities, including but not limited to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), or any federal task force.
All records concerning whether Ventura County or VCSO has enabled, disabled, accepted, rejected, or otherwise participated in any Flock Safety national database or nationwide data-sharing functionality.
All records concerning any requests for or access to Ventura County or VCSO Flock/ALPR information relating to immigration enforcement, immigration investigations, reproductive healthcare, political activity, protests, demonstrations, or other constitutionally protected activity.
8. Flock Community Network and privately owned cameras
All records concerning the County's or VCSO's use of or participation in Flock Safety's Community Network Access or any substantially similar Flock feature.
Records identifying privately owned Flock cameras, including cameras operated by businesses, homeowners' associations, schools, neighborhood organizations, or other private entities, to which County or VCSO personnel have direct or indirect access.
All agreements, authorizations, policies, correspondence, or other records concerning the County's or VCSO's ability to request or obtain access to privately owned Flock camera feeds or Flock-generated information.
Records sufficient to identify the number of requests made by County or VCSO personnel for access to privately owned Flock cameras or feeds.
Records sufficient to identify the number of privately owned Flock cameras or camera feeds available to County or VCSO personnel through the Flock platform.
Records concerning whether privately owned Flock cameras are included in any County or VCSO searchable database, map, network, or investigative platform.
9. Flock Safety system capabilities and configuration
All records describing the capabilities and functions enabled on the County's Flock system, including the types of vehicle information, license plate information, vehicle characteristics, location information, images, alerts, or other data collected.
Records identifying which Flock Safety products, modules, software features, databases, or services are enabled for Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning use or availability of Flock's vehicle search, vehicle fingerprinting, hot-list, alert, sharing, analytics, or other investigative functions.
Records concerning any integration between Flock Safety and other County or law-enforcement systems, databases, records-management systems, computer-aided dispatch systems, camera systems, or investigative platforms.
Records concerning any use of Flock data in connection with facial recognition, biometric identification, person identification, predictive policing, artificial intelligence, or other automated analytical technology.
Records concerning Flock's Vehicle Fingerprint or similar vehicle-identification technology as configured or used by Ventura County or VCSO.
Records concerning automated alerts generated through Flock, including alerts associated with NCIC, NCMEC, hot lists, stolen vehicles, wanted persons, missing persons, or other databases.
10. Effectiveness and results
All reports, statistics, analyses, presentations, or evaluations concerning the effectiveness of the County's Flock program.
Records sufficient to identify crimes, arrests, citations, stolen-vehicle recoveries, missing-person recoveries, investigations, prosecutions, or other law-enforcement outcomes that the County or VCSO attributes to information obtained through Flock/ALPR technology.
Any cost-benefit analyses, performance evaluations, return-on-investment analyses, or assessments of whether Flock cameras have achieved the County's stated objectives.
Any reports or records concerning false alerts, inaccurate plate reads, misidentification, system errors, or other reliability issues involving Flock technology.
Records concerning instances in which Flock information was used to initiate, support, or materially advance an investigation, arrest, search warrant, surveillance activity, or other law-enforcement action.
11. Security and data breaches
All records concerning cybersecurity incidents, vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, data breaches, system compromises, or other security incidents involving the County's Flock system or Flock/ALPR data.
All notices, reports, correspondence, investigations, or assessments concerning any actual or suspected unauthorized disclosure or access to Flock/ALPR information.
Records concerning security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or other security assessments of the Flock system, to the extent such records are not exempt from disclosure.
12. Communications concerning Flock
All emails, memoranda, letters, text messages maintained as public records, meeting notes, and other correspondence between County/VCSO officials or employees and Flock Safety representatives concerning the County's Flock program.
All communications between County/VCSO officials or employees and other governmental agencies concerning Flock Safety, ALPR technology, data sharing, privacy, retention, surveillance, or related issues.
All communications concerning concerns, complaints, objections, privacy issues, civil-liberties issues, or legal issues relating to Flock Safety or the County's ALPR program.
All communications between Flock Safety and the Ventura County Sheriff's Office concerning access to, sharing of, or searches of Flock data maintained by other law-enforcement agencies.
13. Grant-funded cameras and County Service Areas
All records concerning the acquisition, funding, installation, operation, and maintenance of Flock cameras using state, federal, County Service Area, or other grant funding.
All grant applications, grant awards, grant agreements, reimbursement requests, grant reports, and grant-related correspondence concerning Flock Safety cameras.
All records concerning the three Flock license plate readers reported as approved and installed in Oak Park, including records concerning their funding, installation, ownership, operation, maintenance, data retention, and access.
All records concerning any Flock cameras proposed, approved, funded, or installed in Oak Park, Oak View, or any other unincorporated Ventura County community.
All records identifying the governmental entity or department that owns the cameras and the governmental entity or department responsible for the data generated by those cameras.
14. Current status
Records sufficient to establish whether Ventura County and/or VCSO currently intends to continue operating the Flock Safety ALPR program.
All records concerning any proposed renewal, amendment, expansion, termination, suspension, or replacement of the County's Flock Safety contract or program.
Any current Flock Safety contract, renewal agreement, amendment, or other document establishing the County's present contractual relationship with Flock.
Records concerning any change to the County's Flock program, privacy policy, data-sharing practices, retention period, or access permissions since January 1, 2026.
Request for electronic production
Please provide responsive records electronically in their native electronic format where reasonably available, including searchable PDF, Excel/CSV, or other native formats for databases, spreadsheets, logs, and reports.
For records that exist in a database or other electronic system, I request an electronic export of the responsive data rather than screenshots or summaries, where reasonably practicable.
For access logs, audit logs, query logs, event logs, hot-list reports, and similar electronic records, please provide the underlying electronic records in a machine-readable format where reasonably available.
I am requesting existing records and am not asking the County to create a new record or answer questions. Where a requested record is maintained in a database or other electronic system that can reasonably be queried or exported, please provide the resulting electronic record to the extent permitted by the California Public Records Act.
Segregation of exempt information
If the County believes any responsive record contains information exempt from disclosure, please provide all reasonably segregable portions of the record after redacting only the information specifically exempt from disclosure, pursuant to Government Code § 7922.525.
If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon for each withheld record or portion thereof and provide the factual basis for the claimed exemption. Please also identify the name and title/position of each person responsible for the denial, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.
If the County contends that records are exempt under the California Constitution, Government Code, Evidence Code, Penal Code, Civil Code, or any other statute, please identify the specific statutory provision relied upon.
If records are withheld pursuant to the catch-all exemption or another balancing test, please provide the County's specific justification demonstrating why the public interest served by withholding the records clearly outweighs the public interest served by disclosure.
Search and response
Please construe this request broadly to include records maintained by:
• Ventura County Sheriff's Office
• Ventura County Executive Office
• Ventura County Board of Supervisors
• County Counsel
• County Information Technology Services
• County Procurement/General Services
• County Auditor-Controller/Treasurer-Tax Collector, where applicable
• County Service Areas
• Sheriff's Office command staff
• Sheriff's Office investigations/divisions
• Any other County department, division, unit, employee, contractor, or agent reasonably likely to possess responsive records
Please also include responsive records maintained on behalf of the County by Flock Safety or another contractor to the extent those records constitute public records subject to disclosure.
If responsive records are maintained by VCSO rather than the County's central records system, please treat this request as applying to both entities and route the request accordingly rather than requiring a new request.
If the County believes this request is overly broad or requires clarification, please contact me promptly and identify the specific portion that requires clarification rather than denying the request in its entirety.
I request that the County comply with the California Public Records Act's applicable response deadlines, including Government Code § 7922.535.
If responsive records are available on an existing County website, please provide the direct location of those records; however, I request electronic copies of records that are not readily accessible online.
Please preserve all potentially responsive records while this request is pending.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Juiciest

title: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Special Event Overtime Data (Boston Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Special Event Overtime Data (Boston Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

8/27/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records. 

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing the all Time and Labor Reports and Overtime Reports for special events and non-detail non-court overtime records for all Boston Police Department employees from January 2020 through present. Please provide all fields used in the tracking system for these cards, including:
City of Boston Employee ID (6 digit ID)
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number
Rank
District/Taskforce
Assigned description
Charged description
Overtime date
Overtime code and description
Start time
End time
Worked hours
Billed hours
Amount paid

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents. 

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

communications.subject: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: LIHTC Detroit
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Properties located within the City of Detroit that have received, been allocated, reserved or otherwise been associated with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, including federal 9% credits and 4% credits.

For each LIHTC project located in Detroit, please provide the following information, if maintained:

- Project name and any prior or alternate project names
- Complete street address and ZIP code
- Project identification number, application number or allocation number
- Current owner name
- General partner, managing member, developer, sponsor or affiliated entity names
- Number of total residential units
- Number of LIHTC-restricted units
- Credit type, including 9% credits, 4% credits or other applicable category
- Date of allocation, reservation, award, placed-in-service date or other relevant program date
- Credit allocation amount or annual credit amount, if available
- Current compliance or extended-use status, if maintained
- Any recorded expiration, termination, foreclosure, transfer, ownership-change or other status information concerning the project’s LIHTC restrictions

If MSHDA maintains a master list, project inventory, allocation list, compliance database, or similar report containing this information, please provide that record rather than requiring the information to be compiled manually.

The requested time period is from the beginning of the LIHTC program through the date this request is processed. If a full historical search is not reasonably available, please provide the complete records currently maintained by MSHDA and identify the earliest date covered by those records.

This request seeks existing public records and does not require MSHDA to create a new record or answer questions. If the requested information is maintained in multiple records, please provide the records in the form in which they are ordinarily maintained.

If MSHDA determines that the request is too broad or needs clarification, please identify the specific concern and provide an opportunity to narrow or clarify the request before denying it.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Aaron Mondry

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: PRR log MSP
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I request a copy of the Department's existing electronic log or list of the public records requests it has received, including for each entry the date the request was received, a brief summary or description of the request, the name of the requestor, and the status or resolution of the request, for the period January 1, 2024 through the date this request is fulfilled.

I am not seeking law enforcement records, criminal offender record information, or any underlying case files. I seek only the administrative log describing the public records requests your office has received — information of the kind that is frequently available from other public sources.

If the log is maintained electronically, please provide it in its existing machine-readable format (for example, CSV or Excel). Producing the existing electronic export should require no segregation or redaction time.
For your reference, the following may bear on the handling of this request:

- In SPR 17/1115 (December 4, 2017), after in camera review, the Supervisor found that a log describing the public records requests received by the Department is not exempt under the CORI Act or G.L. c. 41, § 97D, and ordered the Department to produce the records unredacted.
- This category of record has already been produced by the Department in unredacted form (SPR 17/1115), which defeats any categorical exemption claim.
- To the extent any privacy exemption under G.L. c. 4, § 7, cl. 26(c) is considered, that interest is overcome where the same information is available from other public sources. See PETA v. Dep't of Agric. Res., 477 Mass. 280, 292 (2017).

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian McCarter

communications.subject: RE: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request #P005953-060126
communications.communication:
Dear Supervisor of Records:

I appeal the Massachusetts State Police's response to my public records request of June 1, 2026, reference P005953-060126, which asked for the Department's existing electronic log of the public records requests it has received since January 1, 2024, in the machine readable format in which it is already kept. A response was due June 15, 2026. The Department's only response came on August 31, 2026, the same morning I wrote to ask about the delay, and its entire substance is this: "Please be advised the Public Records Unit processes requests in the order they are received. Due to the high volume of requests we receive daily, we have not yet had a chance to process your request. We appreciate your patience as we diligently work through this high-volume queue." That is a response, but not the one the law requires. It produces nothing, identifies no records, asserts no exemption, describes no search, assesses no fee, and names no date by which the Department will act. G.L. c. 66, section 10(b) and 950 CMR 32.06(2) require each of those things, and they set the deadline without regard to how many other requests the Department has in its queue. The volume of an agency's own backlog is not a ground recognized anywhere in the statute or the regulations for deferring a response, and a custodian that needs more time must say so within the ten business days and give a good faith date, not answer eleven weeks late with an open ended request for patience. A response that supplies none of the required content is a constructive denial. The record sought is a single existing export of an administrative log, that the law requires them to have, the same category of record the Supervisor ordered this Department to produce unredacted after in camera review in SPR 17/1115 (December 4, 2017). I ask that you find the August 31 letter deficient and order the Department to produce the log within ten business days in its existing machine readable format.
